title: Observed transition matches the native step
statement: Let $M$ be a Boolean-input, Boolean-work-tape machine with state set $Q$, let $s$ be a natural number, and let $c$ be a configuration on a Boolean input $x$. Suppose every work head of $c$ lies within distance $s$ of the origin and every tape cell at distance greater than $s$ is blank; also suppose $c$ is not halted. For any tag $\tau$ and bit $b$, form record data from $c$ and the window of radius $s$, then set its tag to $\tau$, its native-right flag to $b$, and its input field to the symbol read by $c$. The action prescribed from this data, applied to $c$, equals $M$'s one-step successor; its output equals the symbol emitted by $M$ on that step; and the record data's outside flag is false exactly when the successor configuration still satisfies the same window condition.
